title: Gear window on the front face is a messy scatter of copper blocks and glass with
instruction: Clear the area and rebuild with a ring brush: a 9-11 block-diameter circle of copper/cut_copper, a smaller inner glass disc, 4-8 spokes and a center hub. Frame it with a brick or stone arch so it reads as one round window.
why: The window surround now reads as a deliberate stone-and-copper frame with a clearer sill band instead of a scatter of mixed blocks, though a stray copper block still floats inside the glass opening and the gear shape is still hard to read.

title: The right-hand wall on the front-right view is largely open: large rectangular h
instruction: Fill the openings with brick, then cut deliberate windows: framed in stone or copper, 2x3 with glass panes and sills. Keep any loading bay as a single clear opening with a lintel.
why: The right-hand wall was a large rectangular hole showing interior through the wall, and the change fills it with a framed brick panel with a dark recessed window and a stone sill, so the facade reads as a solid, crafted wall instead of a gap. The only minor concern is the new panel's edge sitting slightly proud of the adjacent pipe and valve column.

title: The roof is mostly a flat or lightly stepped oxidized-copper slope with glass st
instruction: Use a sawtooth preset: 3 repeated ridges with vertical glazed faces and sloped copper backs, running side to side. Cap the edges with a continuous stone parapet, and close the hole between the roof and the front wall.
why: The new grey sawtooth blocks add a silhouette the brief asked for, but they read as loose, muddy-grey slabs that clash with the oxidized copper, and they hide most of the glass skylights in the front view, which were the roof's main light feature.

title: The crane and loading door are not legible. The door is a small dark wood block
instruction: Add a 2-wide loading door with a clear lintel. Above it, build a projecting beam (iron bars or fence) with a chain hanging down and a hook. Run continuous copper-pipe lines along the walls, with a valve block (lever or button) at the bends.
why: The loading bay now reads as a wider dark-wood door with a visible central opening and a row of iron rails above it, which is more legible than the lone small block, although the crane itself still doesn't read clearly.

title: Copper accent patches on the brick walls are random and unframed. Stray blocks f
instruction: Run the copper as ordered horizontal bands or riveted panels at regular spacing, and remove floating blocks. Taper the chimney tops with a stepped collar and add a campfire or smoke cap.
why: The scattered copper blocks are mostly gone, leaving a more uniform brick field that reads as one wall, though some copper pillar accents remain and the new brick band above the gable is a plain fill.
